question: Why does putting out every small fire make the big ones worse?
answer: Trees grow, lightning strikes, and fire jumps to touching trees. Most fires are small and a few run far, as in real records. Put every fire out by 10 a.m. and the forest fills up for one giant, because small fires keep it patchy.
move: Small fires keep a forest patchy. Put them all out and it fills up for one giant.

web.label: The 10 a.m. rule. Asks why putting out every small fire makes the big ones worse. Shows a bar chart where each bar is one fire: most bars are small, a few run far. Text covers trees growing, lightning strikes, fire jumping to touching trees, a 45% figure, and the rule to put every fire out by 10 a.m.

source: Veritasium, “You've (Likely) Been Playing The Game Of Life Wrong” (YouTube, 2025)
